taxonomy:
## Taxonomy (by core mechanic), using only the provided rules

### A) Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black/edge; bulbs can’t illuminate each other; each white cell illuminated.
- **Kurodoko**: Color black cells so each number equals the count of white cells from the number to the nearest black cell or frame (horizontally+vertically); numbered cells stay white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.

### B) Black/white (or shaded/unshaded) region formation
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; orthogonally connected black cells must form rectangles/squares; orthogonally connected white cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers give size of the area containing the cell.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms (bold rectangle regions) with numbers = count of painted cells; white cells can’t stretch across >2 rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.
- **Hitori**: No number repeats in any row/column among white cells; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-enclosed territories have numbers indicating how many more marks they get; “—” limited by horizontal/vertical span; “|” limited by vertical/horizontal span.
- **Kurotto**: Color cells black; circle number = sum of continuous black cells extending from it orthogonally; empty circles may have any number; circle cells cannot be colored.
- **LITS**: In each bold area, color four consecutive squares (tetromino); similarly shaped rotated/reflected tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares connected; no 2×2 or larger all-colored squares.
- **Nurikabe**: Fill with white/black; numbers indicate size of continuous white regions; each white region has exactly one number; black cells form a continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2.
- **Nurimeizu**: Shade cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; shaded cells connected across region boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 group entirely shaded.
- **Nuritwin**: (Same family as Nuritwin rules) Shade some cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks orthogonally connected; blocks in same region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 all shaded; shaded cells connected across boundaries.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares (four kinds); cannot place in black squares; uncovered white cells must form rectangle/square; numbers indicate how many black triangles surround it orthogonally.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms (bold) with numbers = count of continuous black cells in that room; rooms with no number any; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; when stones “drop” straight down, stones must fill bottom half without empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-enclosed tiles; color tiles so that diagonal-line cell numbers specify required black cells to the right/down along the line/column until grid edge/another diagonal; all cells in a tile are either all colored or all uncolored; final outline forms an object.
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; cells with numbers cannot be colored; each rectangle bordered by bold lines contains exactly one wrong number (wrong colored-cell count); colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells.
- **Yajilin**: Draw a single loop; loop must not pass through black cells or numbered cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally; (numbers show black-cell count in arrow direction).
- **Yosenabe**: Move circles orthogonally into gray areas; each move shown by straight arrow; arrows don’t bend/cross other circles/lines; number in a gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it; empty gray areas any sum but at least one circle must enter.

### C) Loop / path drawing (single non-self-crossing loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers orthogonally; no crossing/branching/revisiting; must pass all white-circle cells; in each bold-enclosed area, loop either goes straight through all white circles or turns right-angled at all of them; must not go through black-circle cells.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; passes all circles; white circles require straight-through and a right-angled turn in at least one adjacent cell; black circles require a right-angled turn at the circle cell then straight through next cell.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; passes through arrow cells; loop direction follows arrows; wind direction blocks movement against wind; additional constraints when entering wind-blown cells (must move at least one cell; cannot hit borders or enter black cells in that bent movement).
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop through cell centers orthogonally; no crossing/branching/revisiting; must pass all black circles with each black circle as midpoint of the straight segment through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; passes through each room only once; once it leaves a room it can’t return; in each room loop goes through all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); after moons in one room, next room entered must be suns, and vice versa.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; dotted segments between black cells or outer frame are “Gates”; loop must pass all Gates but each Gate only once; loop starts/returns to open numbered circle; open circle number = number of Gates to go through; black cells at Gate ends show when loop crosses; Gate without number can be crossed at any point.
- **Yajilin**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; numbers show black cells in arrow direction; loop does not pass through black cells or numbered cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.

### D) Connectivity / pairing / non-crossing lines (not necessarily a loop)
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges; number of bridges equals island number; max two bridges between islands; bridges can’t cross islands/other bridges; bridges form a continuous link between all islands.
- **Hebi**: Place numbers in snake parts so 1→5 are sequentially connected in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; from 2→1 direction, other snake parts can’t be in squares adjacent to next black square or rim (attack rule); black squares show nearest-square count in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of same numbers with continuous line; lines go through cell centers orthogonally or turning; never twice through same cell; lines can’t cross/branch off; lines can’t go through number cells.
- **Pencils**: Mark pencils; draw lines from pencil tip through cell centers; pencil is straight group of one+ cells with tip at one end; number in pencil cell gives pencil length; line from tip goes through one or as many cells as the number; pencil line can’t cross itself or branch.
- **Satogaeri**: Move circles within bold “countries” so each country contains only one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells they must pass through; circles without numbers may move any distance but some don’t move; circles can’t cross tracks of other circles and can’t go over other circles.
- **Satogaeri** (also fits as “track movement”): same as above.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms (bold) each contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicated in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ the value.
- **Slitherlink**: Connect adjacent dots with vertical/horizontal lines to make a single loop; numbers indicate how many lines surround the cell; empty cells any; loop never crosses or branches off.
- **Nagareru** (also loop-based but includes wind-direction constraints): already listed under loops.

### E) Tiling / partitioning into blocks/regions with shape constraints
- **Chained Block**: Fill black blocks; consecutive black cells form blocks; cell number indicates size of its block; “?” unknown; every block must contain one number or “?”; blocks in corner contact form chains; all blocks part of a chain; chain can’t contain more than one block of one size/shape (rotation/mirror considered same).
- **Double Choco**: Divide grid into blocks by solid lines over dotted lines; each block contains a pair of white-area and gray-area with same form (rotation/mirror allowed); number indicates total cells of that color in block equals half the block’s cells; block can contain any number of cells with the number.
- **Evolomino**: Draw squares in some white cells; orthogonally connected group is a block; each block contains exactly one square placed on a pre-drawn arrow; each arrow must pass through at least two blocks; subsequent blocks on an arrow route must grow by adding one square without rotating/flipping.
- **Five Cells**: Divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells; no blocks with 0–4 or 6+ cells; numbers show how many lines of a block are around the cell (including outer frame); up to 5 numbered cells per block; lines must surround a cell and cannot enter a block.
- **Fillomino**: Fill all empty cells with numbers; divide board into blocks; each block filled with same number horizontally or vertically; each block size equals its number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero** (not tiling; already in connectivity).
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin** (region/block constraints already in black/white).
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles with numbers in cells; each rectangle contains only one number showing number of cells in rectangle.
- **Sashigane**: Divide grid into L-shaped blocks one block wide; all blocks must be L-shaped; open circles form the knee (bend); open circle number indicates number of cells in its block; arrows form one end pointing toward knee; number of marks in a block (arrows or open circles) may be 0–3.
- **Tilepaint** (tile coloring) already listed under black/white.
- **Sto-stone** (rooms) already listed under black/white.

### F) Sudoku / arithmetic grid filling
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with numbers from a list; numbers are either up-down or left-right; one cell has only one digit.
- **Sudoku**: Place 1–9 in each empty cell; each row, column, and each 3×3 bold block contains all numbers 1–9.
- **Makaro**: Fill all empty cells with numbers; bold-enclosed rooms; each room contains all numbers up to the number of cells starting from 1; in black arrow cells, the biggest number among up to four adjacent cells (over/under/left/right) is in the cell the arrow points at; a number can’t be next to the same number in another room.
- **Kurodoko** (numbers as counts) already listed under illumination/visibility.
- **Usowan** (numbers as neighbor counts) already listed under black/white.

### G) Directional/arrow-based movement or constraints (non-loop)
- **Hebi**: Snake territorial/attack constraints based on arrow direction and nearest black square.
- **Nagareru**: Wind direction based on arrows; loop movement restricted against wind.
- **Pencils**: Pencil line direction from tip; length constraints.
- **Satogaeri**: Circle movement along tracks; cannot cross tracks or go over circles.
- **Yajilin**: Arrow direction indicates count of black cells in that direction.
- **Sashigane**: Arrows point toward knee in L-blocks.

### H) “Number indicates local structure” (counts around/within)
- **Akari** (numbers are neighbor counts in given squares).
- **Choco Banana** (numbers indicate size of area containing the cell).
- **Hebi** (black squares show nearest-square count in arrow direction).
- **Kurodoko** (numbers indicate count of white cells to nearest black cell or frame).
- **Kurotto** (circle number = sum of continuous black cells extending from it).
- **Masyu** (circle types impose turn/straight rules rather than numeric counts).
- **Ripple Effect** (numbers impose distance constraints when duplicated).
- **Shakashaka** (numbers indicate black triangles around it orthogonally).
- **Suraromu** (open circle number = number of Gates to go through).
- **Yosenabe** (gray area number = sum of entering circle numbers).

If you want, I can also reorganize this taxonomy into a smaller set of top-level categories (e.g., “loops”, “fill/tiling”, “shading”, “connections”, “arithmetic”) while keeping the same game-to-category mapping.
